title: exakit
tagline: Your local Exasol database and everything that talks to it.

groups.title: Models and UDFs (udf-devkit, hidden for now)

commands.summary: Check this machine's requirements; install nothing.
commands.description: Re-runs the machine-requirement checks the installer runs first - RAM, free disk, the container engine or the macOS runtime, and the ports the database needs - against an installed kit, and changes nothing. The same checks run before an install with EXAKIT_PREFLIGHT=1.

commands.summary: Is the database up and healthy?
commands.description: Shows what is installed, whether each component is healthy, which datasets are loaded, and whether add-on services are running. While the installer is still running the status is `installing` with the current step, exit 3, so a poll started in another shell can follow the install from its first seconds.

parameters.name: --json, -j
parameters.description: Print machine-readable output rather than decorated text.

parameters.name: --help, -h
parameters.description: Show this command reference without installing or restarting anything.

commands.summary: What is installed, and what is newer.
commands.description: Kit source and install date, then one row per component and add-on: what is installed, and whether the maintainers advertise something newer. Applying what is waiting is `exakit update`. --json prints the same rows as one object (installed, advertised, status, severity per component) with the installed/status/remedy keys every state query carries.

commands.summary: Your connection details.
commands.description: The connection panel: DSN, admin and MCP users, where each password file lives, TLS mode and paths. --json prints the install record (manifest.json) plus the state keys installed / status / remedy / skills on stdout, with nothing else on it.

parameters.name: --json, -j
parameters.description: Print machine-readable output rather than decorated text.

parameters.name: --help, -h
parameters.description: Show this command reference without installing or restarting anything.

commands.summary: Friendly walkthrough of every way to connect.
commands.description: How to connect AI clients over MCP, SQL clients (DBeaver or DbVisualizer), the terminal and Python via pyexasol, then where your notebooks, dashboards and models are: the schemas actually loaded, the persona the kit is set up as and the add-ons it has.

commands.summary: Start the database and every add-on service, or one of them.
commands.description: Starts everything the kit runs, deploying the database first if it has never been deployed. Name a service to start only that one: database, or an installed add-on that runs a service (exakit status lists them under services). An add-on needs the database, so exakit start <add-on> refuses (exit 2) while the database is stopped and names the bare command. An unknown or uninstalled service is refused (exit 2) and nothing is started.

parameters.name: <service>
parameters.description: Start only this service. Omit it to start the database and enabled add-on services.

parameters.name: --help, -h
parameters.description: Show this command reference without installing or restarting anything.

commands.summary: Stop the add-on services and the database, or one of them.
commands.description: Your data is kept. Bring it back with exakit start. Name a service to stop only that one - exakit stop exasol-scheduler leaves the database and every other add-on running; the bare command is the only form that stops the database without naming it. An unknown or uninstalled service is refused (exit 2) and nothing is stopped. A stopped add-on that is registered for automatic start comes back at the next login; exakit autostart is where that is turned off. exakit stop database asks first whether to stop the running add-on services too, because they need the database: yes stops them before it, no stops the database alone and names the exakit start <service> each needs once the database is back. EXAKIT_STOP_ADDONS=1 or 0 answers without a terminal; with neither, they are stopped too.

parameters.name: <service>
parameters.description: Stop only this service. Omit it to stop add-on services and the database.

parameters.name: --help, -h
parameters.description: Show this command reference without installing or restarting anything.

commands.summary: Come back automatically after a restart?
commands.description: Shows whether the kit's services start at login, then offers to change it.

commands.summary: Run one SQL statement, with the error translated.
commands.description:
Runs a single statement and turns the three faults everyone hits first into their remedy (connection refused -> exakit start; FETCH FIRST/TOP -> LIMIT; object not found -> describe it). Reads only unless --write. A saved statement runs with --file <path> or on stdin; comment lines (--) and a trailing ; are dropped first. The remedy is printed FIRST, on stdout with the error. --json returns one object instead: {"ok": true, "rows": [...], "row_count": n} or {"ok": false, "error": ..., "remedy": <a command to run as written, or null>, "remedy_hint": <the explanation, or null>}, nothing else on stdout. remedy is only ever a runnable command (exakit start for connection refused, exakit status for a TLS fault); a fault with no command to run (object not found, FETCH FIRST/TOP) has remedy null and its advice in remedy_hint - read it, do not execute it; a refusal (typo, write without --write, two statements) is {"ok": false, "error": ..., "rejected": true} with exit 2. A first word that is neither a read nor a known write is reported as unrecognised (a typo), not as a write.

From Windows PowerShell 5.1, a double quote inside an argument is dropped by PowerShell itself before exakit runs, so a quoted identifier would reach the database unquoted: pass such a statement with --file <path> or pipe it in: 'SELECT "Name" FROM t' | exakit sql. PowerShell 7 keeps the quotes.
commands.warning: This connects with the starter-kit profile, which is the ADMIN user and is NOT sandboxed. The read-only boundary is the MCP user, not this command.
examples: exakit sql --json 'SELECT COUNT(*) AS c FROM TPCH.NATION'

commands.summary: Load a dataset (downloaded only when you pick it), one file, or a whole folder.
commands.description:
Opens the data-loading menu: the bundled datasets (one per folder in data/datasets), your own data, or an external source - the last row runs the exakit connect wizard after the loads, at a terminal only (where virtual schemas cannot run it is shown disabled, with the reason). Name a path to skip the menu, or a bundled dataset by id (exakit data-load amazon_sales) to load just that one.

A FILE asks the same two things whatever its kind - the file, then SCHEMA.TABLE - and JSON is shredded into tables by an engine the kit installs for you (macOS, Linux and WSL; on Windows a folder's JSON files are listed as skipped). Files go to the loader as they are: a ';'-separated CSV with its delimiter, a header with no rows skipped by name, a tabular .txt or .tsv listed with the rename to .csv that exapump needs.

A FOLDER is a bulk load: every CSV / Parquet / JSON (.json, .geojson) file at its top level, one table each named after the file, asking for the schema once. Subfolders are not scanned, files of other kinds are ignored, and duplicates - byte-identical files, or two names that resolve to the same table - are skipped with the reason.

RUNNING AGAIN IS SAFE: a file already loaded is skipped rather than loaded on top of itself, a file a stopped run left half-written is reloaded from scratch, and a target table holding rows this kit did not load is left alone unless EXAKIT_ON_EXISTING says replace or append (on a terminal you are asked). A SINGLE FILE is held to the same rule: declined, it exits 5 with nothing changed, and the same file loaded twice is recognised and left as it is. When the load finishes, every file is listed with its table and the rows it landed, or the reason it did not load; a file the engine refuses leaves no empty table behind.

--force REPLACES bundled datasets instead of skipping what is already there: their tables are dropped and rebuilt, so anything you changed in those schemas is lost; with a dataset id it drops and rebuilds just that one, in either order.

tpch, energy and weather are bundled with the kit and load offline. Every dataset beyond them (amazon_sales, fraud_transactions) is a checksummed archive in the kit's datasets release, downloaded only when it is loaded (GITHUB_TOKEN for a private repository): the kit verifies its SHA-256 and every file's digest, and refuses a mismatch. Unattended, EXAKIT_DATASETS=tpch,energy,weather loads only what is not loaded yet; external among them names the external-source row, which unattended only prints the exakit connect hint.
environment: EXAKIT_DATASETS=tpch,energy,weather names exactly which bundled datasets to load
EXAKIT_DATA_FILE=/path/file.json or /path/folder answers the local-data question, so a run without a terminal loads that file or folder
EXAKIT_DATA_TABLE=SCHEMA.TABLE answers the target-table question for a single EXAKIT_DATA_FILE (default: STARTER_KIT.<filename>)
EXAKIT_SCHEMA sets the default target schema

EXAKIT_ON_EXISTING=skip|replace|append decides what happens to a target table that already holds rows this kit did not load, for a single file and for every file in a folder alike (default: skip, which is also the answer without a terminal; a declined single-file load exits 5 with nothing changed)
EXAKIT_DATASETS_MIRROR=<folder or https base URL> takes the reference dataset archives from there instead of the GitHub release (digests still checked)
EXAKIT_DATASETS_REPO=owner/name is the repository whose releases hold them

parameters.name: <file-or-folder-or-dataset>
parameters.description: Load a CSV, Parquet, JSON/NDJSON file, a folder, or a bundled dataset ID. JSON Tables is selected automatically for JSON.

parameters.name: --force
parameters.description: Reload bundled datasets even if their load receipt already exists; inspect replacement behavior before using it.

parameters.name: --help, -h
parameters.description: Show this command reference without installing or restarting anything.

exit_codes.0: loaded, or everything named was already there
exit_codes.5: a single-file load was declined: the target holds rows this kit did not load

commands.summary: Every log the kit can show.
commands.description: The installer run, the database container, each add-on service, what the boot entries wrote at login, and the virtual-schemas day log (every SQL statement exakit connect and exakit source sent, secrets redacted; kept 14 days). No target lists them all with size and last-updated; -f follows one live; --path prints just the path for piping.

parameters.description: A log ID, for example setup, notebook, notebook-marimo, dash-server, json-tables or udf-devkit-mlflow. UDF container operations are in setup.

parameters.description: Continue showing new lines until Ctrl+C.

parameters.name: --lines N, -n N
parameters.description: Number of existing lines shown before following or returning.

parameters.name: --path
parameters.description: Print the selected log filename without its contents.

parameters.name: --json, -j
parameters.description: List available log targets as JSON. Cannot be combined with a target.

parameters.name: --help, -h
parameters.description: Show this command reference without installing or restarting anything.

commands.summary: Connect your AI clients.
commands.description: Permanently configures the exasol MCP server in every supported AI client. Existing configs are backed up first. Restart the client afterwards and look for a server named exasol. Takes no options: clients are named with EXAKIT_MCP_CLIENTS (an option or argument exits 2). A client whose config no longer holds the kit's entry is offered again.
environment: EXAKIT_MCP_CLIENTS=claude,codex names clients by name (never menu numbers)
EXAKIT_SKIP_MCP=1 skips MCP setup entirely

commands.summary: Test and repair the AI connection.
commands.description: Checks the configured MCP clients, repairs what has drifted - including a warning it can act on, such as a loosened file mode - then re-checks. Confirms the database is running first. --json reports the diagnosis without repairing; its remedy names this command. Each finding names the client it is about, and only that client reads needs_attention.

commands.summary: Show managed MCP state per client.
commands.description: Which clients the kit manages, which config file each one uses, and the current snapshot id. --json prints the operation result with a per-client state list (configured / not_set_up / not_installed).

commands.summary: Remove the kit's MCP entries from named AI clients.
commands.description: Takes the kit's managed entries (exasol, and an add-on's such as dash-server) out of the named clients and forgets them, so mcp-doctor stops reporting a client that is no longer on the machine. Clients by name (claude_desktop, claude_code, codex, cursor, vscode_copilot, gemini_cli, opencode, continue); the full removal is exakit uninstall.

commands.summary: List the AI skills the kit carries.
commands.description: One skill per component and add-on, with a one-line summary and whether each has reached the agents' discovery folders. Names the next command when one is needed: exakit update when the maintainers advertise a newer skill set, exakit skills-install when a placed skill has gone missing. The panel ends with one labelled tally (installed, arriving with an add-on, not placed, total), and --json carries the same four numbers under counts (installed, needs_addon, missing, total; they add up to total) beside installed_version, advertised_version, status and next.

commands.summary: Re-place the AI skills the kit copy carries (repair only).
commands.description: Places the skills this kit copy carries into ~/.claude/skills and ~/.agents/skills, and merges the read-only command allowlist into Claude Code's settings. The installer already does this, and exakit update fetches and places a NEWER set, so this is only for a skill folder that went missing: exakit skills names it when that is the case. Restart or reload the agent afterwards.

commands.summary: Who the kit is set up for - Data Scientist or General: list, show, plan, add or remove one.
commands.description:
A persona is a named set of the answers the installer already takes: which datasets to load, which AI clients to connect, which marketplace add-ons to install. The kit offers two, data-scientist and general, and they combine with a comma (both together load everything).

data-scientist: the Amazon sales and fraud transactions reference datasets (downloaded from the kit's datasets release), every AI client, the dash-server and notebook add-ons. general: the kit's own TPC-H, energy and weather samples (bundled, loaded offline), every AI client.

exakit persona add <id> (apply is its old name) joins the personas named to the ones this kit was set up as and brings in what is not here yet - the sample data, the AI clients, the add-ons - with no question, each step showing the installer's own table (plain lines without a terminal). What is already here is named once and not redone; a part that fails does not stop the others, and the closing line names the command that retries it. With no id, on a terminal, it asks the install's persona question with this kit's personas ticked; without a terminal it names the command instead. --yes is accepted and changes nothing.

exakit persona plan [<id>] shows what the personas bring and what of it is still pending here - with no id, the ones recorded (--json for a script). exakit persona list and show <id> take --json too. exakit persona remove <id> takes a persona off the record and keeps everything it brought.

At install time: EXAKIT_PERSONA=<id>. An answer you give yourself replaces the persona's for that one variable: EXAKIT_PERSONA=data-scientist EXAKIT_DATASETS=amazon_sales loads only that dataset. Personas are files in personas/ (personas/README.md); adding one needs no installer code.

exit_codes.1: a part of persona add did not finish; the closing line names its retry
exit_codes.2: an unknown persona or option, or persona add with no id and no terminal
exit_codes.4: persona add with no kit installed

commands.summary: Optional add-ons: dashboards, notebooks, UDFs, dbt, scheduling and more.
commands.description: Browse and install optional tools: Space selects, Enter installs. Bare and without a terminal it installs NOTHING - installing non-interactively takes an explicit answer. --list shows every add-on and its state without installing anything (--json for scripts: one object whose addons array carries id, status, installed, version, repo and docs - the repository as owner/name and the documentation URL - and name, url and about - the add-on repository's name, link and About on GitHub, as last looked up; version, repo, docs, url and about are null when unknown). The full reference for any add-on is on this machine: exakit help <id>. Naming ids installs exactly those: exakit marketplace dash-server. Installed add-ons then update through exakit update, and one can be removed with exakit uninstall <id>. A tool you installed yourself is recognised and never re-offered.
environment: EXAKIT_MARKETPLACE_ADDONS=dash-server answers the menu non-interactively (ids csv, all, or none)

parameters.name: <addon-id>...
parameters.description: Install only these registered add-ons. Without IDs, open the chooser on a terminal; install nothing without a terminal.

parameters.name: --list
parameters.description: List add-ons and ownership without installing. Cannot be combined with install IDs.

parameters.name: --json
parameters.description: List add-ons as JSON; read-only and cannot be combined with install IDs.

parameters.name: --help, -h
parameters.description: Show this command reference without installing or restarting anything. Combine with --json for structured help.

commands.summary: Open JupyterLab or Marimo, connected to the local database (the notebook add-on).
commands.description: Starts JupyterLab in the background on 127.0.0.1 (port 8888 unless you name one) with the kit's notebooks and the kernel 'Exasol (Starter Kit)', and opens it in your browser, logged in; the login token is a kit credential and is never printed. Every run first writes the kit's current database connection into the notebook connector's encrypted store, so a restart or a port change needs no edit, and copies any kit notebook you do not have yet (yours are never overwritten). check proves the connection and says whether JupyterLab runs, starting nothing; setup settles JupyterLab (yours, or the kit's after a yes) and starts nothing; stop stops the JupyterLab the kit started. JupyterLab is never installed unasked (EXAKIT_NOTEBOOK_JUPYTER=install|skip answers for a script) and never starts with the database or at login. Needs the add-on: exakit marketplace notebook.

parameters.name: <tool>
parameters.description: Open one tool; use at most one. With no tool, show the chooser on a terminal and use JupyterLab without a terminal.

parameters.name: check, --check
parameters.description: Check the environment and database connection without opening a tool.

parameters.name: setup, --setup
parameters.description: Prepare or repair the notebook environment and connection.

parameters.name: stop, --stop
parameters.description: Stop the selected tool, or both notebook servers when no tool is named.

parameters.name: --marimo
parameters.description: A compatibility alias for the tool word. Prefer marimo.

parameters.name: --no-browser
parameters.description: Start the server without opening a browser window.

parameters.name: --port N
parameters.description: JupyterLab/Marimo loopback port, 1024..65535. A running server keeps its current port; stop it first to move it.

parameters.name: --help, -h
parameters.description: Show this command reference; install nothing and change no services.

commands.summary: The workflow logs the notebook helpers write: list them, show one.
commands.description: A notebook starts a workflow with nb.workflow('name') and gets an id, wf-YYYYMMDD-xxxxxx, that it prints with the log's path; nb.workflow(resume='wf-...') continues one from another kernel. While a workflow is active every step the helpers run - a statement (its session and statement ids, its SHA-256 and text), a Langfuse trace, an MLflow run, a descriptor draft or approval, a handoff, a dashboard revision, a model put - appends one JSON line carrying the id to ~/.exasol-starter-kit/workflows/<id>.jsonl, so a result can be traced back through every step that made it. Without a workflow nothing is written. The log never holds a credential: the helpers refuse a password, token, secret or api_key field and a DSN with a password in it. list shows one row per workflow (id, first and last timestamp, line count, name); show <id> prints its lines in order; --json gives the same as JSON. Exit 0; 1 when the add-on is not installed or there is no such workflow; 2 on bad arguments. Needs the notebook add-on, whose helpers write the log: exakit marketplace notebook.

commands.summary: Start or stop the local MLflow server, show its address, or replay pending runs.
commands.description: The server listens on 127.0.0.1, starting at port 5000. Its SQLite store, artifacts, log and pending run spool live under ~/.exasol-starter-kit/mlflow. The notebook add-on supplies the client and the UDF dev kit enables the service. Starting installs the full MLflow server package into the notebook environment if needed. Starting it records that you want it: exakit start brings it back after that, and never starts it for a udf-devkit user who has not asked for it. A plain stop is for the session; exakit mlflow disable (or stop --disable) stops it and keeps it off until the next exakit mlflow start. exakit stop stops the server; exakit logs mlflow shows its log. Replay sends spooled runs to MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI, the kit server, or the local store, and removes only records logged successfully.

parameters.name: <action>
parameters.description: Choose the server operation, or replay pending MLflow run records.

parameters.name: --port N
parameters.description: start only: loopback port for a new MLflow server. An already-running server keeps its current port.

parameters.name: --disable
parameters.description: stop only: also prevent automatic restart with exakit start. The disable action has the same effect.

parameters.name: --json, -j
parameters.description: Print the action result as JSON.

parameters.name: --tracking-uri URI
parameters.description: replay only: send pending records to this MLflow server.

parameters.name: --tracking-dir PATH
parameters.description: replay only: log to a local MLflow store in this folder.

parameters.name: --timeout SECONDS
parameters.description: replay only: server health-check timeout.

parameters.name: --help, -h
parameters.description: Show this command reference; install nothing and change no services.

commands.summary: Draft each column's role in a table (key, time, measure, category, flag, text, identifier, other), then approve it for the notebooks and AI clients.
commands.description: Profiles SCHEMA.TABLE in one pass of SELECTs (the column list, one aggregate statement per 40 columns, then the values of the low-cardinality columns, an exact distinct count of the near-unique ones and the range of date strings; nothing is written to the database) and prints its descriptor. A table whose approved descriptor still matches it (the schema digest of its column names and types) gets that one back - for a dataset the kit ships, the shipped approved descriptor until you approve your own; otherwise a draft: every column gets one of eight roles - key, time, measure, category, flag, text, identifier, other - with its confidence (high, or low when the deciding number was within 10% of its threshold) and the evidence that chose it, and a column whose values look like e-mail addresses, phone numbers, IBANs or postcodes is marked sensitive and is never charted, grouped or sent to a model. The slots name the columns the notebooks use: key, time, text, target - never drafted, only ever set by a person - category and entity; an empty slot says why. The draft is deterministic: the same table gives the same bytes. A virtual table is read as its first 10,000 rows (--sample is accepted and ignored). When EXAKIT_MODEL_ID and EXAKIT_PROVIDER_BASE_URL are set, one call with each column's name, type, role, evidence and top values (never a row, never a sensitive column) adds a one-line note per column; a note never decides a role. The draft is kept in ~/.exasol-starter-kit/descriptors/<SCHEMA>.<TABLE>/draft.yaml with its profile; --json prints it as one object, --write saves the YAML too. When the table changed since its approval, the columns whose name and type did not change keep their approved roles and the rest are flagged. --approve takes a dataset id, SCHEMA.TABLE or a draft file, applies the corrections given as --role <slot>=<COLUMN> (key, time, text, target, category, entity; date and label still name time and target; <slot>=- leaves it empty), checks that every column has a role and none sits in two slots and that the table has not changed since it was profiled, writes v<n+1>.yaml (a version is never rewritten) and current.yaml, status approved, owner --owner (else EXAKIT_DESCRIPTOR_OWNER or the OS user) and approved_at, then publishes the roles: a view EXAKIT_SEMANTIC.<SCHEMA>__<TABLE> naming every column with its role in the column comment (the user's own table is never commented), granted to the read-only MCP user, read back after. A publish that fails leaves the approval standing and says why; --comments publishes again later, --no-comments skips it. Approving what the current version already says writes nothing. --show prints one version (--version n; the current one by default), --versions lists them. --schema <SCHEMA> describes the whole schema at once: every table with its rows and key (a declared primary key, else the first column named like a key that is unique and never empty) and every many-to-one link between them - a foreign key the database declares, or a column that names another table's key (O_CUSTKEY and C_CUSTKEY, CUSTOMER_ID and CUSTOMERS.ID) whose every value is in that key (at most 0.1% missing, checked with one LEFT JOIN; a name alone never makes a link), each with its evidence. The draft is kept in ~/.exasol-starter-kit/descriptors/<SCHEMA>/draft.json; --approve applies --link TABLE.COLUMN=TABLE.KEY and --unlink TABLE.COLUMN, writes v<n>.json and current.json and publishes the links as the view EXAKIT_SEMANTIC.<SCHEMA>__RELATIONS (FROM_TABLE, FROM_COLUMN, TO_TABLE, TO_COLUMN, KIND, EVIDENCE) for agents; the schema's own tables are never altered. The Explore notebook turns an approved map into one joined view (EXAKIT_PREPARED."<SCHEMA>__<TABLE>__JOINED") with its own approved column map. Exit 0; 1 when the notebook add-on is not installed; 2 on bad arguments or roles (the message names the role and the reason); 3 when the table or the id is not there; 4 when the database is not reachable; 5 when another approve took the next version number twice. Needs the notebook add-on, whose Python runs the service: exakit marketplace notebook.

commands.summary: Python or Rust UDFs: install the official Python container (or the pinned Rust one) and prove it (the udf-devkit add-on).
commands.description: python (the default, or EXAKIT_UDF_LANGUAGE): installs the launcher's official Python script language container (alias PYTHON3) when it is missing (--force reinstalls it), then creates and runs a smoke UDF that reports the Python version. rust (--language rust, or EXAKIT_UDF_LANGUAGE=rust): the pinned Rust container from the matrix in versions.json for your database's architecture and version, downloaded once into ~/.exasol-starter-kit/cache/containers (EXAKIT_UDF_CONTAINERS_MIRROR takes it from a folder or base URL instead), verified against its sha256 and size, installed as alias RUST; its smoke UDF arrives with the next kit step. Installing a container restarts the database: you are asked first (--yes answers, and so does a run with no terminal), running add-on services are stopped and started again once the database answers. Needs Exasol launcher 2.3.0 or later. --json prints one object and nothing else on stdout: {"ok": true, "language", "alias", "container": {"url", "sha256", "arch", "db_versions"}, "smoke": [{"package", "version"}]} or {"ok": false, "language", "step", "reason", "remedy"} with step one of select-container, download, verify, install, smoke, so an agent branches on the language and the step. Exit 2 bad arguments (a language that is not python or rust, an unknown option); 3 the smoke UDF found a declared package missing; 4 no container in the matrix for this language, architecture or database version, or the downloaded file does not match its pinned digest (it is removed; run again); 5 not ready (the add-on is not installed, the database is not running, the launcher is older than 2.3.0, the download did not arrive, no disk, the install was not confirmed); 6 the launcher could not install the container (exakit logs); 7 the smoke UDF did not run, or reported a version other than the pinned one.
environment: EXAKIT_UDF_LANGUAGE=python|rust the language the persona install and udf-setup/udf-use set up unless --language says otherwise (default python)
EXAKIT_UDF_ARCH=x86_64|aarch64 overrides the detected database architecture the container row is picked for
EXAKIT_UDF_CONTAINERS_MIRROR=<folder, file:// or https:// base URL> holds the container assets by file name, instead of the release (digests still checked)

exit_codes.0: the container is installed and, for Python, the smoke UDF passed
exit_codes.2: bad arguments: a language that is not python or rust, an unknown option
exit_codes.3: the smoke UDF found a declared package missing
exit_codes.4: no container for this language, architecture or database version, or a digest mismatch (the file is removed; run again)
exit_codes.5: not ready: the add-on, the database, the launcher, the download or the disk; or not confirmed
exit_codes.6: the launcher could not install the container (exakit logs)
exit_codes.7: the smoke UDF did not run, or reported a version other than the pinned one

parameters.description: Choose the script language.

parameters.description: Reinstall even when the official container is already present; causes a database restart.

parameters.name: --yes, -y
parameters.description: Confirm the database restart for container installation.
parameters.default: ask on a terminal; unattended container installs proceed

parameters.name: --json, -j

commands.summary: Install a script language container: the kit's prebuilt one for this database, or a tarball of your own.
commands.description: udf-use default installs the matrix row (versions.json, components.udf-devkit.containers) for the language (--language, else EXAKIT_UDF_LANGUAGE, default python), your DATABASE's architecture (an Apple-silicon Mac runs an aarch64 database, Windows an x86_64 one; EXAKIT_UDF_ARCH overrides) and its version: downloaded once into ~/.exasol-starter-kit/cache/containers (EXAKIT_UDF_CONTAINERS_MIRROR, a folder or base URL holding the file by name, instead of the release), verified against its pinned sha256 and size before the launcher sees it, installed as PYTHON3_ML (python: numpy, pandas, scikit-learn, scipy at the pinned versions, and the smoke UDF compares every package's version with the pin) or RUST (rust). udf-use <container.tar.gz> installs a container tarball under an alias (PYTHON3_CUSTOM unless --alias names one) and proves it the same way; the database restarts (--yes answers the question). --list shows the launcher's containers and which are installed. --json: the same objects as udf-setup ({"ok": true, "language", "alias", "container", "smoke"} or {"ok": false, "language", "step", "reason", "remedy"}, step one of select-container, download, verify, install, smoke) and the same exit codes: 2 bad arguments (not a tarball, not a file, a bad alias, a language that is not python or rust); 3 a declared package missing; 4 no container for this language, architecture or database version, or a digest mismatch; 5 not ready (the add-on, the database, the launcher, the download or the disk; or not confirmed); 6 the launcher's install failed; 7 the smoke UDF did not pass.

EXAKIT_UDF_CONTAINERS_MIRROR=<folder, file:// or https:// base URL> holds the container assets by file name, instead of the release (digests still checked)

exit_codes.2: bad arguments: not a tarball, not a file, a bad alias, a language that is not python or rust
exit_codes.3: the smoke UDF found a declared package missing
exit_codes.4: no container for this language, architecture or database version, or a digest mismatch (the file is removed; run again)
exit_codes.5: not ready: the add-on, the database, the launcher, the download or the disk; or not confirmed
exit_codes.6: the launcher could not install the container (exakit logs)
exit_codes.7: the smoke UDF did not run, or reported a version other than the pinned one

commands.summary: Apply the updates that are waiting.
commands.description: Applies the quick components (kit scripts, exapump, MCP server, pyexasol, the AI skills, installed add-ons) in seconds. When the kit lists setup that only the installer can do and this machine has not finished it (a core task in setup/core/tasks.json, such as the SQL preprocessor framework), the downloaded installer is rerun once - none of the first install's questions again, every component kept at its installed version; with the database stopped that is deferred to exakit start && exakit update. An update that downloads a newer kit hands the rest of the run to it. When it cannot - the new exakit is missing or not executable, or on Windows, where the kit swap is usually staged for the moment the command exits - the run stops there instead: the rest is deferred (status deferred, remedy exakit update), so run exakit update again and the new kit applies it. Coming from 0.2.2, run exakit update twice. A newer skill set published by the maintainers is fetched and installed here too, with no kit release needed. A database change stops the database, so it is only applied for an answer the run was actually given: on a terminal you are asked, and an unattended run defers it with the exact command. Your data is kept either way. --yes (-y) may stand anywhere. --plan, --backup and --apply belong to the staged Personal major upgrade and work only with personal, as in exakit update personal --plan; written first, or with any other component, they are refused with the form that works. --json answers one object instead, with nothing else on stdout: {"ok", "status": updated|current|deferred|blocked|failed, "updated", "deferred", "blocked", "current", "skipped", "ahead", "failed", "remedy", "remedy_hint"}; every screen line goes to the log, nothing prompts, a database change is deferred unless --yes pre-answers it, and remedy names the command that applies what is left. Exit 1 when an updater failed. An unknown option or target is refused (exit 2) and records nothing.
environment: EXAKIT_CONFIRM_RUNTIME_UPDATE=1 pre-answers yes to the database change
EXAKIT_<COMPONENT>_VERSION pins one component by hand
EXAKIT_PERSONAL_S3=0 skips Exasol's S3 for the launcher and uses the GitHub release directly (for a network that blocks the bucket)

commands.summary: Compare or re-pin the database's TLS certificate.
commands.description: The database's certificate is self-signed, so the kit pins it instead: it records the SHA-256 fingerprint (trust on first use) when it deploys or starts its own database, and every client it builds - the exapump profile, pyexasol, the MCP server's EXA_DSN - refuses any other certificate. Without options this shows the pinned fingerprint against the one the port serves now and changes nothing. A mismatch means the database was redeployed outside the kit, or another process answers on the port: --accept records the live certificate and rewrites the clients that hold the pin, after a question (default no when replacing a pin; without a terminal the answer is no). --yes answers it for a script - pass it only with the user's confirmation. --json answers with one object ({"ok", "status", "pinned", "fingerprint", "recorded_at", "live", "matches", "changed", "dsn", "remedy", "remedy_hint"}).
commands.warning: Re-pinning trusts whatever answers on the database port now. Do it only for your own database, never for a process you do not recognise.

exit_codes.0: pinned and matching, nothing pinned yet, or the pin was recorded
exit_codes.3: nothing answers TLS on the database port
exit_codes.5: declined - not confirmed, nothing was changed
exit_codes.6: the live certificate is not the pinned one

commands.options: docker-nano [--container NAME] [--engine docker|podman] [--dsn HOST:PORT] [--user USER] [--password-file PATH] [--yes] [--json]
commands.summary: Copy an older kit's container database into this one.
commands.description: The installer asks about a container database from an older kit exactly once. This is for the machine that answered skip and wants the data after all, and for a container the installer never saw - made by hand with docker run exasol/nano, or by the upstream kit. Every non-system table is copied out while the container runs and restored into the running deployment with its column types preserved; the kit's own bundled sample data (tpch, energy, weather) is left out when it is unchanged, because the kit loads it itself (exakit data-load). When the container publishes the deployment's port, the database is stopped for the copy out and started again before the copy in; a container on another port costs no downtime. Nothing in the container is changed or removed. What is not named on the command line comes from the record the installer kept, then from the old install's own record, then from the machine (which engine knows the container, which port it publishes), then from an older kit's defaults (container exasol-nano, user sys). --json prints one object on stdout: ok, status (done | nothing | declined | failed | partial), container, engine, dsn, copied_out, restored, left_alone, failed, sample_left_out, reason, remedy.
commands.warning: The password never goes on the command line (there is no --password): pass a file with --password-file, set EXAKIT_LEGACY_PASSWORD for a scripted run, or answer the prompt on a terminal. A text column that held an empty string arrives as NULL.
environment: EXAKIT_LEGACY_PASSWORD=... the old database's password for a scripted run (a file via --password-file is preferred)
EXAKIT_LEGACY_READY_TIMEOUT=n seconds to wait for a container this command had to start (120)

exit_codes.0: done, or nothing of yours to copy
exit_codes.1: the copy did not finish - the reason and where the copies are kept are printed
exit_codes.3: no deployment to copy into, or no exapump to copy with
exit_codes.5: declined - not confirmed, nothing was changed

commands.summary: Query an external database from the local one (virtual schema).
commands.description: Connects PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server, Oracle, Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks or MongoDB, Iceberg tables in AWS Glue - or document files in S3 or Azure Blob Storage - as an Exasol virtual schema: the tables stay at the source and queries fetch what they need. Search by name or alias (pg, mssql). `exakit connect <connector> --help` (or `exakit help <connector>`) prints that connector's guide - what it asks for, where to find each value, a connection string to paste - from docs/virtual-schemas/<connector>.md, and `exakit connect --help` lists every connector with what it needs; this page stays at `exakit help connect`. On a terminal, `exakit connect` alone first names this computer's public IP (the address a source on the internet must allow), then opens a menu of the connectors by name (Space ticks several, Enter confirms; their adapter versions and tiers are in exakit source catalog), then one panel per source: first the source's connection string, pasted at a prompt that shows nothing while it is pasted (the hint lists the forms the connector reads, one per line; Enter on an empty line types the fields instead), then shown back with every credential masked (user:****@, password=****, AccountKey=****, sig=****) - Enter uses it, e pastes it again, Esc or n types the fields instead; a password in it is dropped and asked for separately, hidden - then every field with its default, a required one marked with a red * (a plain * without colour) - Enter takes the default, a required field is never left empty - each answer checked where it is typed, and a numbered summary where a number asks that one answer again (- takes an optional one back). A plan that refuses one input goes straight back to that field; one naming several reopens the summary, where skip leaves that source out. A terminal without the panels asks the same questions line by line, marked the same way, the connection string first (read hidden, shown back masked, the same Enter, e or Esc/n choice). A review shows what each will download and who can read it, and after one question a table follows every source to its VS_<NAME> or its failure; unattended, give every input with --set and the credential with --password-file or --password-stdin (never as an argument). --password-stdin reads all of standard input, line breaks included (a JSON key file), even when a terminal is open; a terminal or an empty stdin is refused (exit 2), and so is --password-stdin with --password-file. A --password-file or --password-stdin credential is read as UTF-8 (with or without a byte-order mark) or as UTF-16 by its byte-order mark, its trailing line endings dropped; anything else, a NUL byte included, is refused, never guessed. Windows PowerShell 5.1 pipes only ASCII to a command, so give a non-ASCII credential there with --password-file. --url takes the source's connection string (a JDBC URL, postgres://, mongodb+srv://, s3://, an Azure blob URL, ...) and fills the inputs it names, each checked as if given with --set; an explicit --set wins over it. A password in the string is never used or stored - the credential is still asked for separately - and settings the kit does not read are dropped by name. The adapter and JDBC driver are pinned and SHA-256 verified; the credential lives only in the database's CONNECTION EXAKIT_SRC_<NAME>, and the tables appear as VS_<NAME>. For a source on the internet the plan also names this computer's public IP address - the one its security group, firewall or IP access list must allow, since the database's traffic leaves through this computer (asked once of checkip.amazonaws.com, at most 3 seconds, never a step; --dry-run --json carries it as public_ip, null when not known) - and a connect or exakit source check that cannot reach the source names it in the fix. A failed connect leaves nothing behind. A source that moved (a new host, port or database) is re-pointed with the same command and its credential again: exakit connect <connector> --name <its name> --set host=<new host> --password-file <file> updates it in place - the recorded inputs stand and what is given replaces them, and VS_<NAME> keeps its name, so saved queries keep working. The credential is always required (a hidden prompt on a terminal, --password-file or --password-stdin unattended; without it, exit 2): the database never returns a stored one, and changing a CONNECTION's address clears it. The new address and credential are tried on a pending connection before anything changes, and any failure puts the source back as it was (exit 1, with the kind and fix); one interrupted part way is put back by the next command on the source. The plan shows each change, old -> new; a terminal asks (No by default), unattended it needs --yes, and --json without --yes changes nothing (exit 5, kind declined). The same inputs and no credential: nothing to change, exit 0 (1 when the source is not ready). A name another connector holds is a conflict (exit 3); a mapping, CA or TLS level is not changed in place, nor is a BigQuery source; a host of localhost is refused as for a first connect; a credential given with --set is refused (exit 2). The first connect installs the Java language container if it is missing (one database restart): at a terminal at once, picking the source being the permission; unattended only with --yes. --json prints one JSON object on stdout and nothing else, on every path: the plan with --dry-run, the connect result (action: connected, reconnected, repointed or unchanged; a re-point adds changes and credential: required in the plan, replaced in the result), or a failure {"ok": false, "error": <what happened>, "kind": <its class: input, conflict, gated, auth, tls, unreachable, nojava, ...>, "remedy": <the fix, in words>, "command": <the one exakit command that is the fix, or null>, "public_ip": ...} - the keys exakit source check --json answers with. It never asks: the credential comes from --password-file, from --password-stdin, or, on macOS and Linux, from standard input without the flag - read to its end, so a pipe that is closed once the credential is written; a stdin that stays open waits forever - and a missing language container is installed only with --yes. Exit 2 bad input, 3 name or object conflict, 5 connector gated or not confirmed (nothing changed), 20 Java in the database has no DNS resolver and the repair connect runs by itself (then one retry) did not fix it, 21 (Java) or 23 (Rust) a language container is missing and was not installed (--yes installs it), 22 the local database did not answer, 1 any other failure.
environment: EXAKIT_CONFIRM_RUNTIME_UPDATE=1 pre-answers the Java container install (--yes does the same)
EXAKIT_NO_IP_LOOKUP=1 skips the public IP lookup (no request to checkip.amazonaws.com)
examples: exakit connect pg --name sales --set host=db.example.com --set database=sales --set user=reader --password-file ~/.sales.pw
pass show db/sales | exakit connect pg --name sales --set host=db.example.com --set database=sales --set user=reader --password-stdin --yes --json

commands.summary: List, check and manage connected external sources.
commands.description: list shows saved sources: where each lives, its TLS level (verify, require or disable) and its last known state (--json rows carry host and tls); issues filters the failing ones with the command that fixes each; check runs a fresh bounded read through the adapter (--all for every source, one shot, not monitoring); reauth replaces the credential from a hidden prompt, --password-file or --password-stdin (all of standard input, as exakit connect reads it) and reads again; refresh re-reads the source's table list; describe lists its tables and columns as Exasol sees them, read from the local catalog without reaching the source, and --ddl prints CREATE TABLE statements (with --schema, for that schema) to copy a table locally; disconnect drops only the CONNECTION (queries fail until you connect again with the same name); remove drops the virtual schema, adapter and connection and deletes the downloaded files no other source still uses. disconnect and remove preview first and ask; --dry-run only previews, and without a terminal or with --json they need --yes (unconfirmed: exit 5, nothing changed; with --json the answer is kind declined and command names the --yes form). reauth tries the new credential before it replaces the old one. Remote data is never touched.
examples: exakit source describe sales orders --ddl --schema LOCAL > orders.sql
layout: Remember two commands:
exakit source               pick a source from the list
exakit source <name>        its card, and everything you can do with it
That is all you need. The commands below do the same things directly -
for scripts and AI agents (each takes --json), or if you prefer typing.
exakit source <command> [options]
Observe
list                          Every saved source, its TLS level and last state
issues [--status S]           Only the failing ones, each with the command that fixes it
show <name>                   One source: inputs, objects, type and naming notes
describe <name> [table]       Its tables and columns as Exasol sees them
[--ddl] [--schema S]       --ddl prints CREATE TABLE to copy a table locally
catalog                       Every connector the kit can connect
Check and fix
check <name> | --all          A fresh test read through the adapter (one shot)
refresh <name>                Re-read the source's table list (new tables appear)
reauth <name>                 New password or token - tried before it replaces the old
[--password-file F | --password-stdin]
[--storage-secret-file F]  a lakehouse source with two secrets: both, always
Remove
disconnect <name>             Drop only the connection (connect again to restore)
remove <name>                 Drop the schema, adapter and connection, and unused files
[--dry-run] [--yes]        preview only / no question asked
Every command: --json for one machine-readable answer. Remote data is never touched.
Examples
Observe
exakit source list                              all sources at a glance
exakit source list --json                       the same, for a script or an AI agent
exakit source issues                            only what is broken, with the fix
exakit source show sales                        everything about one source
exakit source describe sales                    its tables
exakit source describe sales orders             one table's columns
exakit source describe sales orders --ddl --schema LOCAL > orders.sql
CREATE TABLE to copy it into Exasol
exakit source catalog                           which connectors exist
Check and fix
exakit source check sales                       is it working right now?
exakit source check --all                       test every source
exakit source refresh sales                     new tables in the source? show them
exakit source reauth sales                      new password, asked hidden
exakit source reauth sales --password-file ~/sales.pw
cat ~/sales.pw | exakit source reauth sales --password-stdin
Remove
exakit source disconnect sales                  pause it (connect again to restore)
exakit source remove sales --dry-run            preview what would be removed
exakit source remove sales                      remove it (asks first)
exakit source remove sales --yes --json         remove from a script, no question
Related
exakit connect postgresql --name sales --set host=new.host --password-file ~/sales.pw
move a source to a new host (keeps its schema)
exakit connect postgresql --help                what a connector needs, and where to find it

environment.name: EXAKIT_PERSONA
environment.effect: A named set of answers (personas/<id>.json): data-scientist or general, or both joined with a comma (ml-engineer ships in the files but is not offered in this release). It fills EXAKIT_DATASETS, EXAKIT_MCP_CLIENTS and EXAKIT_MARKETPLACE_ADDONS where you did not set them; an unknown persona is refused before anything is installed.

environment.name: EXAKIT_MCP_CLIENTS
environment.effect: Which MCP clients to configure, by name: claude, claude_desktop, claude_code, codex, cursor, vscode_copilot, gemini_cli, opencode, continue, all, skip.

environment.name: EXAKIT_DATASETS
environment.effect: Which bundled datasets to load, by id: one per folder in data/datasets (tpch, energy, weather, bundled and loaded offline, and the downloaded datasets amazon_sales, fraud_transactions).

environment.name: EXAKIT_LOAD_SAMPLE
environment.effect: 0 skips data loading, 1 loads the bundled sample.

environment.name: EXAKIT_MARKETPLACE_ADDONS
environment.effect: Answers the marketplace offer: ids csv, all, or none.

environment.name: EXAKIT_REUSE_DB
environment.effect: 1 adopts an existing database (default), 0 destroys it and deploys fresh - 0 removes the local deployment and all its data.

environment.name: EXAKIT_DB_PORT
environment.effect: Alternate database port. The launcher selects and remembers the deployment's own port; exakit info shows the one in use.

environment.name: EXAKIT_VERSION_POLICY
environment.effect: manifest (default), latest, or pinned - where component versions come from.

environment.name: EXAKIT_CONFIRM_RUNTIME_UPDATE
environment.effect: 1 pre-answers yes to stopping the database for a runtime update.

environment.name: EXAKIT_NO_UPDATE_NOTICE
environment.effect: 1 never prints the update notice other commands can show.

environment.name: EXAKIT_NO_IP_LOOKUP
environment.effect: 1 skips the public IP lookup exakit connect and exakit source check make for a source on the internet (one HTTPS request to checkip.amazonaws.com, at most 3 seconds); the plan and the fix then do not name the address.

environment.name: EXAKIT_PERSONAL_S3
environment.effect: 0 skips Exasol's S3 bucket for the Personal launcher and downloads the verified GitHub release directly - for a network that blocks the bucket. Default: S3 first, GitHub as fallback.

environment.name: EXAKIT_UDF_LANGUAGE
environment.effect: python (default) or rust: the UDF language the ml-engineer persona install, udf-setup and udf-use default set up unless --language says otherwise. Anything else is refused: the UDF language must be python or rust.

environment.name: EXAKIT_UDF_ARCH
environment.effect: x86_64 or aarch64: overrides the detected database architecture the prebuilt container row is picked for (an Apple-silicon Mac runs an aarch64 database, Windows an x86_64 one). For tests and unusual machines.

environment.name: EXAKIT_UDF_CONTAINERS_MIRROR
environment.effect: A folder, file:// or https:// base URL holding the prebuilt container assets by file name, used instead of the GitHub release (offline or internal copies). Size and sha256 are verified all the same.

troubleshooting.symptom: Podman is installed but not running
troubleshooting.remedy: Run: podman machine start - then re-run the installer.

troubleshooting.symptom: Podman cannot apply the pids limit
troubleshooting.remedy: A rootless machine under WSL 2.9+ has no pids cgroup controller (podman-container-tools/podman#29909). Make it rootful: podman machine stop; podman machine set --rootful; podman machine start - then re-run the installer. The kit names this; it never switches the machine itself.

Windows 11 22H2+: add dnsTunneling=true under [wsl2] in %USERPROFILE%\.wslconfig, then: wsl --shutdown; podman machine start (this stops every WSL distro). Older Windows: podman machine stop; podman machine set --user-mode-networking; podman machine start. The kit names this; it never edits .wslconfig itself.

Read its error: podman inspect --format "{{.State.Error}}" <exasol-db-...>. The kit shows it on a failed deploy or start; a pids error is fixed by a rootful machine (see above). A deployment that never started holds no data, and the installer offers to replace it (EXAKIT_REPLACE_DB=0 keeps it).
Stop the other app, or re-run with EXAKIT_DB_PORT=8564.
Re-run the same install command. It resumes from the failed step.
exakit status, then exakit mcp-doctor, then restart the AI client.

troubleshooting.symptom: Another setup run is already in progress
troubleshooting.remedy: Wait for it. If the pid is dead, remove ~/.exasol-starter-kit/.install.lock and re-run.
exakit logs has the full story. Every error message names its remedy.
